$comment: SecretLoop configuration template. Copy to .secretloop.json. Both the VS Code extension and the CLI read this file, so the editor and CI never disagree about what counts as a finding. Only .secretloop.json is read; there is no fallback to any other filename.
$comment_excludePaths: Added to the built-in excludes (node_modules, lockfiles, minified bundles, dist) — you never need to re-list those.
$comment_excludeRules: Rule ids to disable project-wide. Use when a rule is structurally wrong for your stack, not to silence one line — for that, add `secretloop:allow` on the line instead.
$comment_allowValues: Regexes matched against the detected value. Use for fixtures and documented sample credentials.
$comment_entropyPassEnabled: Set false to report only named-format rules and drop the generic high-entropy tier. Cuts noise hard on codebases full of hashes and base64 fixtures.
$comment_keyContextRequired: Set true to make the generic high-entropy tier report a QUOTED value only when the identifier it is assigned to carries a secret-like word (apiKey, db_pass, sessionToken). Off by default: it cuts noise, and what it costs in missed credentials depends on how your repository names things. Unquoted values are never gated. Same as the --key-context flag.
$comment_generatedExcludePaths: Replaces the built-in generated-file group (lockfiles, wrappers, SARIF reports) rather than adding to it. Empty here means keep the shipped list; --include-generated scans them for one run.
$comment_includePaths: Restricts the scan to these globs when non-empty. Empty means scan everything the excludes leave.
$comment_includeFixtures: Set true to report generic-tier findings in test, fixture and example paths. Named provider rules already fire there regardless, because a real token in a test file is a real leaked token.
